Alerting and notification delivery

The proactive alert engine evaluates health checks every 15 minutes and routes each finding to five sinks — in-app bell, e-mail, a signed webhook, integration hooks and a syslog/CEF feed — each with its own severity floor and family mask.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSettings → System → General → Email & Alerts (alert engine: satom-alerts.timer)

What is it?#

Every other monitoring page is pull: you open it and read it. The alert engine is push: a systemd timer (satom-alerts.timer) runs it every 15 minutes on every node; it evaluates a set of health checks and sends each new finding to the people and systems that asked for it, so nobody has to be looking at a page.

What does it do?#

Checks#

Check (label) Raises a finding when… Family
Cert expiry this node's TLS certificate has ≤ Cert warn (days) left, or a renewal failed cert
Git divergence the standby lags more than Git behind max commits, or a local commit stays unpushed longer than Git unpushed max (hours) git
Device health a device is degraded or critical on the same ladder as Device health, plus a live TCP probe of its port (devices in maintenance are skipped). One finding per device, listing every failing signal — not one per signal. When a deep monitor is behind it, the title carries the reading and the limit crossed (Device {device} is critical — CPU 97.0% (critical 95%)) and the body lists each alerting probe with what it measures, the last reading, every limit with where it is set (on the probe, inherited from the product, or factory default) and when it was read; six are spelled out, the rest counted device
Signature database (3.0) a FortiWeb's signature database is older than alerts.signature_max_days (default 7), reports it never updated, or its version could not be read by the daily signature_check — device.signature_stale / device.signature_unreadable, warning. See Signature freshness device
Backup freshness the newest database bundle (local or off-box) is older than Backup stale (hours) backup
Config drift a device's harvested configuration changed within Drift window (min). Live state the appliance reports inside its configuration (FortiADC virtual-server/pool/interface availability, certificate OK/Expired status) is not configuration and never raises it drift
Intent deviation (3.4.0) an appliance bound to an approved template no longer matches it: the template is rendered with the device's variables and compared field by field with the cached device objects. One warning per binding, keyed intent.<device>:<binding>:<hash>, naming the fields that differ and never a value. On by default, with its own toggle intent
Scheduled automation an enabled scheduled action keeps failing or is overdue; or a SATOM process (web, scheduler, reconciler) has run code older than the files on disk for more than 15 minutes actions
Host resources this node's disk, memory or load is degraded host
API catalog integrity an object disappearance points at SATOM's own endpoint catalog catalog

A failure of the engine itself becomes an engine finding; a finding with an unrecognised key prefix belongs to family unknown. No filter can drop engine or unknown.

Drift is not intent deviation. Config drift says the device changed since its previous snapshot; a device that drifted weeks ago and has been stable since raises nothing. Intent deviation says the device does not match what it is bound to, however long ago it stopped matching. The comparison is the key-subset diff the template approval modal uses, never equality against a raw snapshot: an appliance fills in fields the template never set, counts its own sub-table rows and renumbers internal handles, and none of that is a deviation. Sub-table rows are reported unmeasured rather than guessed at. Maintenance mode and the drift exclude list silence the check exactly as they silence drift. The same verdict appears as the Compliance column of the bindings table in the Template library, and hooks can subscribe to the typed event intent.deviation (Integrations). In NAF terms this is the Observability block's event "when the actual state differs from the intended one" — see Where SATOM sits in the NAF Framework.

Sinks#

Sink Default Notes
In-app bell on, info, all families to every admin-capable user; ignores the master switch
Email on, info, all families needs Enable alert dispatch; one mail per run
Webhook (HTTP POST) off needs the master switch; one POST per run with every accepted finding
Integration hooks off needs the master switch; one alert.fired event per finding — enqueued, not delivered
Syslog / CEF feed off no cooldown, runs on the standby too, ignores the master switch

Each sink has exactly two filters: a Minimum severity (info, warning, critical) and Families delivered. A sink with no family ticked delivers nothing, and the page says delivers nothing.

Cooldown#

A finding that reached at least one notification sink is suppressed for Cooldown (hours) (default 6). The syslog feed has no cooldown. Device and host findings include the status in their key, so an escalation from warning to critical is delivered even inside the cooldown.

Requirements#

  • satom-alerts.timer enabled on each node (see Services and timers).
  • SMTP configured on the same tab for e-mail.
  • A webhook URL, a syslog collector, or an integration hook bound to alert.fired for the respective sinks (hooks: see Integrations).

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Saving alert settings and Preview now (no send) require users.manage (Administrator); others get 403. The tab is in the admin-only System › General sub-menu of Settings (the Monitoring & Alerts group until 3.5.0). Bell notifications go to users who can administer users.

How to use#

Turn alerting on safely#

  1. Open Settings → System → General → Email & Alerts.
  2. Configure SMTP in Email (SMTP) Configuration, Save email settings, then Send test (it uses the saved settings).
  3. In Alerts & notifications, fill Alert recipient(s) (blank falls back to the e-mail default recipients) and tick the Checks enabled.
  4. Adjust the limits (table below) and the Delivery sinks rows.
  5. Click Preview now (no send): it evaluates every enabled check and shows what would fire, the resolved recipients, the count per sink and, per finding, which sinks accept it. Nothing is sent.
  6. Tick Enable alert dispatch and click Save alert settings.

Set up the webhook#

  1. In Webhook endpoint, enter the Endpoint URL, choose Encoding (SATOM envelope or Slack-compatible {"text": …}), Timeout (s), Retries, and optionally a Signing secret (HMAC-SHA256).
  2. Enable the Webhook (HTTP POST) sink row, then Save alert settings.

The secret is stored encrypted and never shown again; a blank field keeps it, Remove the stored secret deletes it. It follows the vault mode (Settings → Vault). A secret that is set but cannot be read shows unreadable — deliveries go unsigned; deliveries still go out, without X-SATOM-Signature, and their result says sent UNSIGNED.

Set up the syslog / CEF feed#

In Syslog collector (FortiAnalyzer, SIEM) set Collector host, Port, Transport (UDP or TCP), Encoding (RFC 5424 or CEF) and Facility (local0–local7); enable the Syslog / CEF feed sink row and save.

Configuration#

Field Description Default
Enable alert dispatch Master switch for e-mail, webhook and hooks off
Alert recipient(s) Comma/newline list; blank = e-mail default recipients —
Cert warn (days) Certificate runway that raises a finding 14
Cooldown (hours) Per-finding suppression after delivery 6
Git behind max Commits the standby may lag 25
Git unpushed max (hours) Age of an unpushed local commit 6
Backup stale (hours) Maximum age of the newest database bundle 48
Drift window (min) Only drift newer than this alerts 90
Change made through SATOM Report it, credited to its author (info), Report it as drift, credited to its author, Do not report it report, credited
Automation fail streak → critical Consecutive failed scheduled runs that make it critical 3
Automation overdue (hours) How late an enabled action may be 3
Device alert floor Degraded and worse or Critical only Degraded and worse

Webhook delivery#

Item Value
Headers X-SATOM-Timestamp (epoch seconds), X-SATOM-Delivery (stable id per batch), X-SATOM-Signature: v1=<hex> only when a secret is set
Signed string v1:<timestamp>:<raw body> with HMAC-SHA256
Retries 408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 and transport errors are retried with 1 s, 3 s, 7 s backoff; any other 4xx fails once
SATOM envelope version, source, event, id, node, sent_at, count, max_severity, findings[] (key, family, severity, title, detail, product)

Verify the signature against the raw request body before parsing JSON. The webhook card on the page shows the exact sample payload for the selected encoding.

Syslog / CEF severities#

SATOM severity Syslog CEF
critical 3 9
warning 4 6
info 6 3

RFC 5424 uses the family as MSGID. The CEF header carries the node's local time (it has no timezone field) and rt= carries epoch milliseconds.

Example#

🧪Example — Critical device alerts to a chat room, everything to the SIEM

  • Webhook (HTTP POST): on, Minimum severity critical, families Device health only, Encoding Slack-compatible, URL of your chat incoming webhook.
  • Syslog / CEF feed: on, Minimum severity info, all families, Transport TCP, Encoding CEF, collector siem.example.com.
  • Preview now (no send) confirms a degraded device would reach the syslog sink only, and a critical one both.

Result#

  • Saving writes an audit entry (Updated alert/notification settings).
  • Each run prints a summary to the journal (journalctl -u satom-alerts). A run that found something and reached nobody exits non-zero, so the unit shows failed.
  • If the engine cannot run at all (for example the database is down), the wrapper script logs the machine's disk, memory and load to the journal and syslog without needing the database.

Troubleshooting#

A device is red and no mail arrived#

Check in this order: 0. satom get alerts status → last email. REFUSED means the engine tried and the mail transport said no (a local relay answering 454 Relay access denied, for example); the status is bad until a send gets through. Fix the transport, then Send test. deliverability: ERROR means the mail was delivered, but unsigned and straight to the recipient's server: look in the spam folder (see below). 1. Enable alert dispatch (the bell and the feed ignore it; e-mail does not). 2. The e-mail sink's Minimum severity and Families delivered. 3. Device alert floor (Critical only hides degraded devices). 4. The cooldown — the same finding may have been delivered in the last hours. 5. Preview now (no send) — it shows which sinks accept the finding.

"Deliverability error": the mail is delivered but may land in spam#

Settings → Email shows a red Deliverability error box, Send test adds a red line after a successful send, and satom get alerts status reads deliverability: ERROR with status bad. The local mail server (Postfix, no relayhost, no signing milter) hands each message straight to the recipient's mail server with no DKIM signature. It is accepted, and Gmail, Outlook and others may file it as spam, where nobody reads an alert.

  • The From address needs an SPF record that authorises the node's public address; without it Gmail refuses the message outright (550 5.7.26 … the sender is unauthenticated).
  • Mark the first alert Not spam in the recipient's mailbox.
  • To clear the error: External SMTP server with a provider account, or a relayhost / DKIM milter on the node.

"Alert settings saved." but nothing is evaluated#

Check that satom-alerts.timer is enabled on the node (systemctl status satom-alerts.timer).

"hooks: sink enabled but no hook is bound to alert.fired"#

The hooks sink is on but no integration hook subscribes to alert.fired. Create one (starters for Telegram, Slack and Microsoft Teams exist on the Integrations page) or turn the sink off. Nothing is stamped in this case, so the finding is not silenced.

"email: no recipients configured"#

Fill Alert recipient(s) or the e-mail default recipients.

"in-app: no admin recipients — nobody holds the bell"#

No user can administer users, so nobody receives bell alerts.

Webhook "fails once" with a 4xx#

The receiver refused the request (wrong URL, rejected signature). It is not retried. Check the URL and the shared secret.

The standby sends no mail#

By design: on a read-only standby only the syslog feed runs; notification is done by the writable primary.

Advanced#

Advanced Not implemented

Syslog over TLS, the LEEF encoding, per-recipient routing (the mask is per sink) and vendor-specific webhook adapters (Teams, Discord, Opsgenie — use an integration hook instead) are not available.

Advanced Command line

flask alerts-run (as used by the timer) accepts --dry-run (evaluate only, send nothing) and --force (ignore the cooldown). Settings live in the application settings table under alerts.*; the cooldown state is the JSON value alerts.state.

Advanced Delivery accounting

dispatched counts findings delivered to the bell, a successful e-mail or a successful webhook. Hooks are counted as queued, never delivered; the syslog feed is never counted. Only delivered or queued findings start a cooldown, so a finding that reached nobody is retried on the next run.
